title: Operator manages jobs from the CLI
description:
The CLI cannot see jobs at all. `auritus` has login, logout, config, deploy,
site, player, worker, and killswitch -- there is no `job` command group. An
operator debugging a wedged clip has to hand-craft curl calls with a Cognito
bearer token, which is exactly what happened in auritus-294fa6.

The admin routes already exist for list and inspect; delete, regenerate, and
retry arrive with the API stories in this epic. This story is the CLI surface
over all five.

## Feature

```gherkin
Feature: Managing jobs from the command line

  Scenario: Operator lists recent jobs
    Given jobs exist with several statuses
    When the operator runs "auritus job list"
    Then each job is printed with its content hash, status, and backend

  Scenario: Operator filters jobs by status
    Given jobs exist with several statuses
    When the operator runs "auritus job list --status failed"
    Then only failed jobs are printed

  Scenario: Operator inspects one job
    Given a job exists with status "done"
    When the operator runs "auritus job show" with its content hash
    Then the job text, backend, voice, timings, and audio url are printed

  Scenario: Operator deletes a job from the command line
    Given a job exists with status "done"
    When the operator runs "auritus job delete" with its content hash and confirms
    Then the job is deleted

  Scenario: Deleting a job asks for confirmation
    Given a job exists with status "done"
    When the operator runs "auritus job delete" with its content hash and declines
    Then the job still exists

  Scenario: Operator regenerates a job from the command line
    Given a job exists with status "done"
    When the operator runs "auritus job regenerate" with its content hash
    Then the job status is "pending"

  Scenario: Operator retries a failed job from the command line
    Given a job exists with status "failed"
    When the operator runs "auritus job retry" with its content hash
    Then the job status is "pending"
```

## Implementation brief

**`cli/src/auritus/api.py`** — add the read methods to match the admin routes:
`list_jobs(status=None, limit=None, next_token=None)` -> `GET /admin/jobs`,
and `get_admin_job(content_hash)` -> `GET /admin/jobs/{hash}`. The mutating
methods are added by their own stories in this epic.

**`cli/src/auritus/commands/job.py`** (new) — `app = typer.Typer(help=...)`
with commands `list`, `show`, `delete`, `regenerate`, `retry`. Follow the
existing shape in `commands/site.py`: catch `AuritusApiError`, print to stderr
in red, `raise typer.Exit(code=1) from exc`.

- `delete` takes `--yes` to skip the `typer.confirm` prompt.
- `retry` takes `--force` for a live claim.
- `list` takes `--status` and `--limit`.

**`cli/src/auritus/cli.py`** — `app.add_typer(job_cmd.app, name="job")`.

**Do not use a bare `typer.Argument`** for the content hash. See
auritus-b0f217 item 2: `--help` crashes on Argument-based commands in this
environment (`TyperArgument.make_metavar()` signature mismatch). `cli.py` has
a compatibility shim for it, but confirm `auritus job show --help` actually
renders before declaring done -- that shim is why `site revoke --help` was
reported broken.

**`features/`** — extend `job_management.feature` or add
`cli_job_management.feature` with the scenarios above.

## Acceptance

`make check` green; `auritus job --help` and every subcommand's `--help`
render without traceback.

comments.text: Implemented on feature/cli-job-commands, merged to develop. Added auritus job list/show/delete/regenerate/retry, plus list_jobs()/get_admin_job() client methods (delete/regenerate/retry methods already existed from prior stories). Uses --hash as an Option throughout, not a bare Argument, avoiding the Argument make_metavar --help-crash class entirely. 17 unit tests including explicit --help-does-not-crash coverage for every subcommand. One real gap noted, not blocking: 'job list' has no --next-token, so the CLI cannot page past the first result page even though the API supports it -- worth a fast-follow. While reviewing this branch I found test_site_revoke_help_does_not_crash failing on bare develop (unrelated to this branch) -- typer/click had drifted in the shared environment since auritus-b0f217 fixed this, to a version where the compat shim's delegate (click's base Argument.make_metavar) no longer accepts the ctx/usage arguments the shim forwards to it. Fixed directly on develop (764ecdb): delegate to typer's own TyperArgument.make_metavar instead, which already handles ctx/usage correctly in the current environment; only backfill ctx for the zero-arg call. All verification re-run after rebasing onto that fix: black/ruff, pytest (54 passed), behave (24 features, 94 scenarios), manual --help checks for all 5 subcommands.
